title.narrative: ECHO Binational HTI-DR - Parent

description.narrative: SUMMARY With the escalating humanitarian crisis in Haiti on one side, and the growing deportation measures taken by the Dominican government on the other side, many children and their families are facing immense adversity on either side of the island. Increased armed violence are causing mass displacement in Haiti, exposing children and adolescents to growing risks, and hampering access to education. Deportations are causing acute protection risks, from family separation to heightened risk of child labour, SGBV and acute emotional distress. The project aims to provide immediate and life-saving protection and education support to the people most in need, targeting children, adolescents and their families in the Haitian communes of Anse-à-Pitres, Jacmel and Bainet, and the Dominican provinces of Elias Piña at the border, as well as La Altagracia’s Verón. The project runs for 24 months from the 15th of May 2025 until the 14th of May 2027 in Haiti and the Dominican Republic.

The principal objective of this action is to strengthen the protective environment and to ensure access to quality child protection services and education services for children, adolescents and their families affected by violence, migration and deportation measures in the Dominican Republic and Haiti. The proposed Action adopts a three-pronged approach: firstly by directly responding to urgent child protection needs with quality child protection case management, the deploymentof adaptive psychosocial support, including through mobile units to reach the most underserved communities, and creating a generally more protective environment through community protection mechanisms. Secondly, in line with the HIP, the action will contribute to the prevention (and where possible stopping) of the worst humanitarian consequences of human rights violations by supporting locally-led humanitarian advocacy, while providing much needed monitoring and documentation support for evidence-based awareness raising, as well as comprehensive binational coordination for case management and referals. Finally, in Haiti protection efforts are integrated with emergency education interventions to ensure children are able to access education services.

This project aims to work with children, adolescents and their families affected by 1) armed violence and displacement and/or 2) affected by migration and deportation measures. The project aims to reach 10 993 unique beneficiaries (without double counting), the large majority of which are children and adolescents between 5-17 years old. In Haiti, the bulk of the project's direct beneficiaries are through Child Protection in Emergencies activities, which are estimated to reach a total of 5628 beneficiaries, of which 78% are children and adolescents (5-17 years old). Building on child protection activities, out-of-school chidlren will be identified for the program's Education in Emergencies activities in Haiti, which will reach 1740 unique beneficiaries. In the Dominican Republic, the core of the response is in Child Protection in Emergencies, which will reach a total of 2903 unique beneficiaries, with the majority (67%) being children and adolescents (5-17 years old).

With longstanding presence in both countries, the proposed Action leverages synergies and complementarity of Plan’s existing and past programs and relations with local and national authorities, working groups, and partners. In Haiti, the proposed Action complements Plan Haiti ‘s (PiH) Emergency Response Plan (2024-2027) which coordinates interventions across Child Protection in Emergencies (CPiE), Education in Emergencies (EiE), and Food Security sectors. In the Dominican Republic, the project is implemented in collaboration with Dominican partner OBMICA. Both Plan Haiti and Plan Dominican Republic are united under Plan's Caribbean Strategy (2025-2029), which maximizes impact through shared goals and collaborative approaches for vulnerable Children, Adolescents, and Youth across the island. This established coordination provides a strong foundation for effective binational humanitarian programming, leveraging coordination mechanisms, shared learning processes, and complementary technical expertise that enable seamless cross-border operations.

With the escalating humanitarian crisis in Haiti on one side, and the growing deportation measures being taken by the Dominican government on the other side, Haitians and people of Haitian origin are facing immense adversity on either side of the island. Increased armed violence are causing mass displacement in Haiti, exposing children and adolescents to growing risks, and hampering access to education. Deportations are causing acute protection risks, from family separation, to heightened risk of child labour, SGBV and acute emotional distress

Quality teaching and learning
Number of girls and boys provided essential learning materials for basic education

description.narrative: The minimum package of learning materials to be defined by partners based on the project focus. This should ensure that basic supplies of textbooks (or equivalent), reading materials and stationery are available to learners. Learning materials to include adaptations and modifications for learners living with disabilities where needed, and tailored to the language needs identified. Where learning kits are provided per classroom, a breakdown of content must be provided to justify reasonable provision per child. Materials may be supplied directly by the project or support (logistical/technical/advocacy/other) may be provided to education authorities to facilitate provision. Disaggregation of data by sex, NFE type or level of education (primary, lower secondary, upper secondary) and disability to be provided.
